sources.entry: QOwnNotes - Plain-text file notepad and todo-list manager with markdown support and ownCloud / Nextcloud integration.

summary.one_liner: QOwnNotes is an open source Markdown notepad and todo-list manager for GNU/Linux, macOS and Windows that stores notes as plain-text files and syncs them with Nextcloud or ownCloud.
summary.what_it_does: QOwnNotes is a desktop notepad that edits plain-text and Markdown note files in user-chosen folders, with markdown highlighting, a live preview, inline image previews and heading folding. It can name notes after their first line and rename files when that line changes. Todo lists can be managed through the Nextcloud/ownCloud Tasks backend or any CalDAV server. With the optional QOwnNotes Nextcloud app, it adds note version history and trash restore, and it supports sharing notes on the server. The README also lists encryption of notes (AES-256 built in, or custom methods such as PGP), scripting with an online script repository, built-in AI support with OpenAI and Groq, and an MCP server for external AI agents. Notes can be synced by Nextcloud/ownCloud file sync, Syncthing or Dropbox, and Evernote and Joplin imports are available.
use_cases: take plain-text markdown notes on the desktop
keep notes synced with a Nextcloud or ownCloud server
edit and search notes from a mobile device via sync
migrate notes from Evernote or Joplin
encrypt individual notes with AES-256 or PGP
notable: Plain-text markdown files that work with other sync tools and existing note folders
Optional Nextcloud app adds versioning, trash restore and note sharing
Built-in MCP server lets external AI agents search and fetch notes
Wiki-style note links with auto-completion, backlinks and refactoring
Low resource use, described as not an Electron app
caveats: Versioning and trash restore require the QOwnNotes Nextcloud app; legacy QOwnNotesAPI servers are still supported
Building from source needs Qt and qtwebsockets, and Windows builds should use MinGW 64-bit
The README includes a no-warranty disclaimer ('as is')
